comparison: Both evaluate the experimental paradigm design (C25-C31) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on methodological details (sample size, conditioning, controls), while peer reviewers praised it as 'highly effective.' Peer review also includes C80 (overall effectiveness), showing broader scope.

Both find behavioral outcomes (C32-C37) SUPPORTED. OpenEval details statistical tests and effect sizes, while peer reviewers confirmed 'clear impacts on pain ratings.' Peer review also includes correlation findings (C38-C40), which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

OpenEval evaluates correlation analyses (C38-C40) as SUPPORTED but notes causal interpretation concerns. Peer reviewers grouped these with primary behavioral outcomes and found them SUPPORTED without expressing reservations about causal claims.

Both evaluate variability analyses (C41-C47) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the 'dynamic updating' interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers also include control condition analyses (C121-C122) and acknowledged these 'speak against alternative explanations.'

Perfect claim overlap (C48-C51). Both find SCR physiological validation SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes reduced sample size (n=26) as a limitation, while peer reviewers emphasized these as 'objective markers' supporting manipulation effectiveness without expressing concerns about power.

Both evaluate SIIPS analyses (C52-C58) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the lack of placebo-control difference as 'somewhat inconsistent' but overall supportive. Peer reviewers also include anticipation null findings (C59-C60, C81-C83) and praised SIIPS as 'an excellent manipulation check,' finding evidence 'convincing.'

OpenEval evaluates anticipation null findings (C59-C60) as SUPPORTED, noting the interpretation about 'distinct processes' is reasonable but preliminary. Peer reviewers grouped these with SIIPS findings and found them central to demonstrating 'substantially different neural representation' between phases.

Both evaluate main fMRI findings (C61-C68) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the 'general and nonspecific' interpretation goes beyond spatial data. Peer reviewers also include related claims (C69-C71, C84-C85, C124) and stated evidence is 'convincing,' representing 'a step forward.'

OpenEval evaluates angular gyrus finding (C69) as SUPPORTED but notes functional interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers grouped this with broader fMRI findings and found the overall pattern convincing without specific comment on angular gyrus.

OpenEval evaluates interpretive synthesis (C70-C71) as SUPPORTED but notes 'different processes' versus 'different states' cannot be definitively distinguished. Peer reviewers included these in their broader acceptance of the temporal dissociation findings.

Both evaluate EEG-fMRI multimodal analyses (C72-C76) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes negative correlation interpretation requires careful consideration. Peer reviewers praised the 'integration of fMRI with EEG' and noted concerns about BOLD-EEG correlations were addressed in revision.

OpenEval evaluates EEG-fMRI synthesis (C77-C79) as SUPPORTED but notes functional significance of correlation directions needs more explanation. Peer reviewers grouped these with the broader multimodal findings and found them commendable for tracking temporal transitions.

OpenEval evaluates paradigm effectiveness summary (C80-C81) as SUPPORTED but notes potential selection bias. Peer reviewers included C80 with experimental design evaluation and praised the paradigm as 'highly effective' without expressing concerns about excluded subjects.

OpenEval rates functional role claims (C84-C86) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative and not directly tested. Peer reviewers rated these UNCERTAIN, with one expressing reservations about specific interpretations (e.g., 'more of a node in a system') and noting fMRI resolution limitations.

OpenEval rates predictive coding framework claims (C88-C90) as UNCERTAIN, noting data don't uniquely support this theory. Peer reviewers grouped these with other interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the framework while questioning specific mechanistic assumptions.

OpenEval evaluates DLPFC literature and timing claims (C91-C94) as SUPPORTED, though causal interpretation goes beyond correlational data. Peer reviewers included these in their SUPPORTED evaluation of theoretical framing, affirming the study makes 'a step forward in understanding.'

OpenEval evaluates DLPFC top-down control claims (C95-C97) as SUPPORTED but notes temporal ordering is suggestive rather than definitive. Peer reviewers grouped these with interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN, expressing reservations about specific mechanistic inferences.

OpenEval rates ACC functional interpretation (C98-C100) as UNCERTAIN, noting highly speculative mechanistic claims. Peer reviewers grouped these with other interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN, questioning whether differential responses should wait for stimulus valence.

OpenEval rates gamma oscillation claims (C101-C103) as UNCERTAIN, noting C103 is highly speculative about expectation transfer mechanisms. Peer reviewers grouped these with interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN, though they included C101-C102 in their SUPPORTED theoretical framing (R10).

OpenEval evaluates insula timing claims (C104-C106) as SUPPORTED, though functional role is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers grouped these with interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN, expressing reservations about the insula as 'a center for coding potential pain.'

OpenEval rates insula mechanistic speculation (C107-C109) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are highly speculative theoretical interpretations. Peer reviewers grouped these with other interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN, acknowledging limitations of fMRI techniques for observing sub-circuits.

OpenEval rates angular gyrus functional role (C110-C112) as UNCERTAIN, noting C112 is highly speculative. Peer reviewers grouped these with interpretive claims rated UNCERTAIN without specific comment on angular gyrus interpretation.

Perfect claim overlap (C113-C120). OpenEval finds methodological justification SUPPORTED while acknowledging control condition limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with one in 'slight disagreement' suggesting the neutral condition 'resembles more of a medium condition' or reflects 'certainty versus uncertainty.'

OpenEval evaluates control condition validation analyses (C121-C122) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers grouped these with variability analyses and acknowledged they 'speak against alternative explanations,' finding them SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates overall synthesis (C123-C127) as SUPPORTED but notes some functional inferences are speculative. Peer reviewers grouped these claims with interpretive statements rated UNCERTAIN, though they accepted the overall framework.

OpenEval evaluates final synthesis (C128-C129) as SUPPORTED, noting conclusions are well-supported by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers included C128 in their SUPPORTED evaluation of theoretical framing, affirming the study's contribution to understanding.

Peer reviewers provided a comprehensive SUPPORTED evaluation of the theoretical framing and literature review (C1-C24, C87, C91-C93, C98, C101-C102, C105, C111, C123, C128). OpenEval did not provide a consolidated evaluation of these background/literature claims, instead addressing them within context of specific findings.
